exposure: nonmedically indicated induction of labor at 39 weeks of gestation
cohort: 630,485 singleton, nonanomalous deliveries in California between 2007 and 2012
finding: Compared to expectant management, nonmedically indicated induction of labor at 39 weeks gestation was associated with lower odds of cesarean delivery in women ≥35 years old, higher odds of operative vaginal delivery in all age groups, and improved neonatal outcomes in all age groups.
